author: Chris Titus Tech
description:
Everyone seems to be hyping Omarchy. I'm not switching to it, but some of its ideas are absolutely worth stealing.

In this hands-on review, I dig into DHH's take on Arch Linux and Hyprland: the plugins, polished theming, helpful menus, and opinionated defaults. I cover what impressed me, what I'd remove, and why my own desktop takes a different direction.

Then I show my Fedora setup with DWM, X11, and Quickshell, including the ideas Omarchy inspired me to bring into my own workflow.

That's the beauty of Linux: keep what you like, change what you don't, and build something that works for YOU.

Which Omarchy feature would you steal for your own desktop? Let me know in the comments.
